chapter_name: Chapter 19: Short Writing Skills Notices Messages and Dialogue
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the formats of short compositions, learning to convey maximum information in minimum words through Notices, Messages, and Dialogues.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Sometimes, less is more! How do you inform a whole school about an event in just 50 words? How do you leave a quick note for your mom? Let's master the art of being brief, clear, and to the point! 📌

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A Notice is a formal announcement. It MUST be placed inside a box! It follows a strict format: Name of Institution, the word 'NOTICE', Date, Heading, Body (What, When, Where, Who), and your Name/Designation. Always write in the third person (no 'I' or 'You').
examples_or_templates: Body tip: Include the 5 Ws - What is the event? When is it? Where is it? Who can participate? Whom to contact?

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A Message is a brief note left for someone who wasn't there to take a phone call or receive information directly. Like a notice, it goes in a box. It only needs: the word 'MESSAGE', Date, Time, Salutation, a crisp Body (only essential details, no new info), and the Writer's name.
examples_or_templates: Body: Ramesh called. His birthday party is at 6 PM today at his house. He wants you to bring the board game. I am going to football practice. - Ravi

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Dialogue is a written conversation between two or more people. It should sound natural and lifelike. Use contractions (I'm, can't), proper punctuation, and keep the exchanges relatively short. Start with a brief greeting and end with a logical conclusion.
examples_or_templates: Shopkeeper: Good morning! How can I help you today?
Customer: Good morning. I'm looking for a blue ink pen, please.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which of the following MUST always be drawn around a Notice and a Message?
❓ In Notice writing, which point of view should ideally be used?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write a catchy, 3-4 word heading for a Notice about a lost water bottle on the school playground.
subjective_practice.hint: Keep it bold and clear. E.g., 'LOST! LOST! LOST!' or 'Lost Water Bottle'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Draft the body of a Message (under 30 words) to your brother telling him that his friend Rahul called to cancel their movie plan.
subjective_practice.hint: Don't add extra fluff. Just state who called and what the message was.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the first two lines of a dialogue between a teacher and a student who is submitting their homework late.
subjective_practice.hint: Start with a respectful greeting from the student and a question from the teacher.

activity_or_assignment.title: ❄️ The Fridge Message
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Imagine you have to leave for school early, and your family is still sleeping. Write a 'Message' on a piece of paper telling them where your keys are and reminding them to feed the dog. Stick it on your fridge!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Notices are formal, strictly formatted announcements that must be enclosed in a box.
⭐ Messages are brief, informal notes relaying exact telephone or verbal information to someone who was unavailable.
⭐ Dialogue writing should mimic natural speech, using proper punctuation and contractions.
